title: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent regional-failover thrashing
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Fixes a race in SLO enforcement backoff ordering that could trigger repeated regional failover/load-shedding cycles under bursty traffic. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: during a production incident on 2026-02-18 we observed repeated regional failovers and cascading load-shedding across dedicated pools. Root cause analysis traced the symptom to the SLO enforcer's backoff ordering: concurrent backoff decisions were non-deterministic and could escalate multiple regions into aggressive backoff simultaneously, which forced traffic to fallback regions and caused thrashing. This hotfix makes the ordering deterministic, adds hysteresis, and tightens the quorum for declaring a region in backoff to prevent simultaneous escalation.

Summary of changes: 1) Enforce deterministic ordering in slo_enforcer: compute backoff candidates, sort by stable key (region id + priority) before applying backoff so retries are applied in a consistent order. 2) Add hysteresis window (configurable via feature flag) so a region must sustain an SLO breach for two evaluation windows before entering aggressive backoff. 3) Increase quorum threshold for regional failover decision to 2/3 of coordinator replicas to reduce flapping during transient partitions. 4) Add metrics and traces: slo_enforcer.backoff_applied (tags: region, reason, level), slo_enforcer.hysteresis_triggered, slo_enforcer.quorum_votes. 5) Add unit tests and integration test in perf-canary that simulate staggered breaches and verify stable failover behavior. 6) Small docs update in redwood-docs explaining the backoff hysteresis flag and recommended tuning.

Checklist: - [x] Repro case & root-cause analysis (attached incident postmortem link: https://linear.app/redwood/incident/INC-2026-02-18) - [x] Implementation with tests - unit + integration in perf-canary - [x] Local and staging canary run (staging run id: canary-20260222-5) - [x] Metrics added and dashboards updated - [x] Rollout plan documented - [x] Add feature flag for hysteresis (default on for this hotfix)

Testing and validation: unit tests cover ordering and hysteresis logic (slo_enforcer_test::OrderingDeterminism, slo_enforcer_test::HysteresisWindow). Integration test added to perf-canary simulates a three-region cluster with controlled latency spikes; expected result is at most one region entering aggressive backoff and no repeated cross-region fallback within 10 minutes. Staging canary ran for 6 hours under a synthetic spike profile and showed stable behavior. CI pipeline initially failed on a race in test harness; the harness was adjusted and CI passed on the final run.

Deployment & rollout: deploy to small percentage of dedicated pools first (10%), monitor slo_enforcer.backoff_applied metrics and region failover rate. If no regressions after 2 hours, increase to 50% and then full. The change is behind a feature flag (slo_enforcer.hysteresis.enabled) so rollback can be performed by toggling the flag. Full code rollback plan: revert the merge and redeploy (low-risk, stateless change).

Backwards compatibility and safety: no API surface changes. The hysteresis window is opt-out via feature flag. We increased quorum threshold for failover decision, which is a conservative change to avoid flapping. No schema or compatibility changes to persisted state.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4580: long-term: evaluate adaptive hysteresis based on request burstiness and traffic profiles - ENG-4622: extend similar ordering guarantees to the regional backoff coordinator path - Add an alert that fires when slo_enforcer.backoff_applied spikes across multiple regions within 5m

Related: Linear ENG-4521, Support SUP-7821.
